### Loop 4 — 2026-10-09 · H1/H2
- **D-H1a — preview server is allow-list only.** scripts/workspace_server.py serves: `/` (generated homepage), gabriel_homes/{templates,static,docs}/ (browsable), gabriel_homes/{DEPLOY.md, DESIGN.md, WORK.md, requirements.txt, README*}, scripts/preview_site/{index,plan,checklist,qa}.html. Everything else → 403. A hard deny-list (any dot-file component, .env*, *.sqlite3, *.db, *.log, *.pyc, cookies.txt, __pycache__, download/, upload/, node_modules/, media/) runs independently of the allow-list so future allow-list edits can never leak those paths. Rationale: this server fronts a public preview link; earlier ad-hoc servers either showed only preview_site or had no principled boundary at all.
- **D-H1b — scripts/ reachable only for the four preview pages + assets.** The four HTML pages are the owner-facing purpose of the server; the rest of scripts/ is agent tooling (code, logs, cookies, scratch dirs) with real leak value and no preview value. scripts/preview_site/qa-shots/*.png is served ONLY because qa.html embeds it (the QA page renders broken otherwise); the qa-shots folder itself stays unlistable (403). Enforced in code, not config.
- **D-H2 — two export zips, two policies.** (1) gabriel-homes-oneclick.zip (customer deliverable) intentionally ships the seeded demo db.sqlite3 so the first run skips seeding; it now EXCLUDES .git/ and real .env (rsync previously leaked the whole repo history) and asserts .env.example/.gitignore/docs in staging and inside the finished archive. (2) gabriel-workspace-snapshot.zip (owner workspace export) must contain gabriel_homes/.env.example, .gitignore, docs/STATUS.md, docs/AGENT-BRIEF.md, manage.py and must NEVER contain db.sqlite3, download/, upload/, scripts/server.log — scripts/check_export.sh exits 1 and names each violation. unzip -Z1 (zipinfo names mode) is used instead of parsing unzip -l columns: same tool, exact filenames, no whitespace parsing.

Placeholders neither satisfy a check silently nor get auto-replaced by the agent; they stay visible until Brian fills them. ### Loop 14 — 2026-11-01 · Owner tree merge + detail map completion (D-MAP-DET)
- **D-MAP-DET · The property detail map joins the search map on self-hosted MapLibre GL + OpenFreeMap positron — the OSM iframe embed is gone.** The Codex tree shipped the detail page with an openstreetmap.org/export iframe plus an orphaned MapLibre detail-map.js (its #detail-map target WAS the iframe, and the script tag had been removed leaving an empty {% if %} stub — unfinished work). Finishing the GL version wins over keeping the iframe: one rendering stack for both maps, one vendoring convention, no external frame dependency (openstreetmap.org availability/rate limits), no frame-src carve-out in the CSP, and the same graceful-degradation story. The outbound "Open in OpenStreetMap" link stays — it is an <a>, not a frame. CSS: the dead Leaflet control rules became MapLibre theming; #detail-map keeps its 400px height; loading/error fallback text styled inside the container. static/vendor/leaflet/ (396K) now has zero code references — left on disk for a deliberate future cleanup rather than silently deleted (S10's vendoring decisions live in this file, so removal should too).
- **D-MAP-RST · "Show all homes" reset pill restored on the search map.** The Codex rewrite of search-map.js dropped the reset the redesign had; with fitBounds-on-load only, a visitor who pans into one neighbourhood had no way back. The pill is created in JS (CSP-clean, no inline handlers), overlays the stage top-left, calls the same fitBounds as the initial frame, and is hidden until more than one pin exists (a single-pin map starts perfectly framed).
- **D-CSP-FRAME · frame-src removed from the CSP.** With the detail iframe gone the site frames nothing at all (verified live: zero <iframe> elements on every smoke page), so the policy reverts to frame-ancestors 'none' only. Tiles stay single-host: tiles.openfreemap.org in img-src + connect-src, worker same-origin/blob per the MapLibre ESM worker. Pinned by the rewritten test_csp_allows_map_tile_hosts_only.
- **D-VENDOR-SRI · No SRI integrity attributes on the vendored MapLibre ESM module.** Dynamic import() (the mechanism both maps use via data-maplibre-src) does not honour SRI — a hash on the tag would be security theatre. The files are same-origin under script-src 'self'; the real guards are the vendoring hygiene test (no sourceMappingURL → collectstatic survives — both .mjs bundles were stripped this run) and the vendor-files-on-disk test. If the module ever moves back to a plain <script> tag, pin SRI then (r13's approach).
- **D-MERGE-14 · The owner's Codex tree is the lineage of record.** Two parallel trees existed after run 13 (the r12/r13 tree and the owner's Codex tree). The Codex tree won on recency (freshest dev DB, lead-listing gallery + video, demo nearby amenities) and on the map implementation (one renderer instead of Leaflet+bridge). The r12 hardening was ported in wholesale rather than rebased, and the LOOP records (STATE, BRIEF §14, this file) now tell both lineages honestly: run 13's approach is documented as superseded, not erased.

### Loop 16 — 2026-11-05 · F2 capability gate shipped (D-LOOP-16)
- **D-LOOP-16a · fx-gate.js is the single capability decision point.** One tiny deferred script sets `html[data-fx]` ∈ {rich, lite, none} (reduced-motion ⇒ none; Save-Data / ≤4 cores / ≤4 GB ⇒ lite; else rich) and `html[data-fine]` on (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). motion.js and bento-shift.js no longer check prefers-reduced-motion or pointer media queries themselves — a pytest guard pins fx-gate.js as the ONLY JS file allowed to mention prefers-reduced-motion. CSS @media (prefers-reduced-motion) token blocks stay: they zero out transition durations (CSS parity layer), they make no decisions.
- **D-LOOP-16b · Fail-closed both ways.** With JavaScript blocked the gate never runs, no attribute exists, and no effect script activates (D-MOTION-SAFE unchanged: reveal CSS still only under html.motion-ready). If fx-gate.js itself is blocked/stale, motion.js and bento-shift.js read the missing data-fx as "none" — effects off, content fully visible. base.html loads the gate OUTSIDE {% block scripts %} so child templates (all call {{ block.super }}) can never drop it; the <html> tag must never hardcode data-fx (guard test).
- **D-LOOP-16c · Bento shape-shift is now rich-tier + fine-pointer only, and under fx=none it does not run at all.** Today's reduced-motion path still promoted the hovered card with an instant (unanimated) layout change; the runbook's "no effect runs under none" cuts that too — under none the grid behaves exactly like a touch device (plain cards, no promotion, no reflow). lite devices (Save-Data / ≤4 cores / ≤4 GB) also skip it. The viewport half of the old check (min-width 1021px) stays local to bento-shift.js — it is layout, not capability, and H3 builds on it.

### Loop 23 — 2026-11-05 · G2 audited MET-T1 + L1 map & list sync (D-LOOP-23)
- **D-LOOP-23a · L1 sync is delegated, oob-announced, and never fights the map for focus.** Row↔pin pairing rides a stable identity (`id="listing-row-<pk>"` + `data-listing-pk` on rows; `"id"` added to the map JSON) so HTMX row swaps need no re-binding — one delegated `mouseover`/`mouseleave` pair on `#results-grid` drives the pin `.is-hot` highlight, and pins (already keyboard buttons) scroll to + `.is-flashed` their row on activation. The flash animation is killed under both prefers-reduced-motion (CSS block) and `data-fx="none"` (attribute rule); scroll behaviour reads `html[data-fx]` (D-LOOP-16a: search-map.js carries no motion-preference query). Focus policy: pin activation opens the maplibre popup, which takes focus itself (`focusAfterOpen`) — that popup link is the keyboard path; flashRow deliberately does NOT move focus (an E3 first pass proved the two fight; the popup won). The result count is `#results-count` with `aria-live="polite"`, and the HTMX partial re-sends it with `hx-swap-oob="true"` so filter/sort changes announce without a full page load. The "Map" pill ships hidden in markup (no dead control with JS blocked, Q3), is revealed by an IntersectionObserver when the map leaves the viewport, scrolls back under the same fx rule, and returns focus to the focusable map region (`tabindex="-1"`). E3 15/15 with live tiles (scripts/r23_e3_l1_audit.py); map-adjacent rgba pulses follow search.css precedent (F1 counts hex literals only, rgba() untouched).

### Loop 26 — 2026-11-05 · F4 audit correction + L2 basemap palette (D-LOOP-26)
- **D-LOOP-26a · The F4 audit hunts exhaustively, and its find is fixed in-audit, not churned.** The r26 effect hunt enumerated every `@keyframes` in static/css (9) plus all JS animation surfaces and found the r25 addendum mapped only 7 hooks: `detail.css gallery-count-bump` (a public detail-page effect → now the M5 confirm row's where-used) and `manage.css manage-card-in` (owner-portal utility UI → declared portal-scoped under Cut/dormant, not silently absent). Fixed in-audit per the D-LOOP-22a precedent (a 2-line doc correction; demoting and rebuilding across two runs would churn the loop for 2 lines), and test_f4_motion_vocab.py's SHIPPED_TOKENS gained both hooks so the coverage gap cannot silently reopen. Auditor D8 docked to 3 (lower-wins); F4 MET-T1. Anchor smooth-scroll (motion.js scrollIntoView) was considered and deliberately excluded from the vocabulary — it is default navigation behaviour that item F5 owns replacing, not a loop-shipped effect.
- **D-LOOP-26b · The L2 "guarded layer list" is an ordered rule list over the loaded style, and the palette is vintage-atlas from runtime tokens.** Exact third-party layer ids drift between style versions, so the recolour enumerates `map.getStyle().layers` at load and applies an ordered `[id-pattern, paint-property, tokens.css-variable]` rule list: first matching rule wins per paint property (casings before generic roads), every application is guarded by `map.getLayer(id)` + try/catch (missing ids never match; layers without a paint property are skipped — never fatal). Colours are read at runtime via `getComputedStyle` from tokens.css — zero hex in JS, so the palette follows any future token change automatically. Mapping: background/landcover/park → `--paper`; water/waterway + buildings/casings/railways → `--sand`; roads → `--cream`; labels/boundaries → `--taupe` text on `--paper` halo. The result (E3 screenshot r26-e3-l2-map-region.png) reads as a vintage-atlas Mombasa — sand ocean and creeks, paper land, cream roads, taupe labels — replacing the positron blue/grey clash. The SVG fallback asset and the single maplibre attribution control are untouched; the price pin stays on `var(--font-sans)` (F1 fix, pinned by test).

### Loop 27 — 2026-11-05 · L2 audit + G1 floating pill nav (D-LOOP-27)
- **D-LOOP-27a · The nav hide/return is functional navigation UI, not a motion-vocabulary family — and the breakpoint moves to 1024px.** G1's hide-on-scroll-down / return-on-scroll-up is an orientation affordance in the same class as the mobile-menu open/close (functional toggles carry no addendum row; adding one would breach the 6-family cap F4 enforces). It is implemented as a JS-only class (motion.js setupNavAutoHide): called ONLY behind the F2 gate (`if (!fxNone) setupNavAutoHide()` — lite or rich), rAF-throttled passive scroll listener, 4px hysteresis, 160px depth threshold, transform-only CSS (`.site-header.nav--hidden { transform: translateY(-100%); }` — no display:none, no layout shift), and a focusin listener that always returns the header for keyboard users. D-MOTION-SAFE holds: with JS blocked or under fx=none the class never appears, so the header is permanently visible (E3-verified all three modes). The full nav and the hamburger handover move from 1200px to 1024px together (SCORECARD G1 contract "full nav from 1024px up"); 1024 is a media-query constant, not a tokens.css value, so no token entry is needed. The 6 inline styles in the header include moved to classes (.mobile-menu__index, .mobile-menu__signout, .mobile-menu .site-header__brand span) — the F1 survey counts px literals only, so the em sizes that moved into CSS are ratchet-neutral (survey re-run: 43 / 215 held).

### Loop 29 — 2026-11-06 · L3 audit + F5 smooth scroll (D-LOOP-29)
- **D-LOOP-29a · Lenis is vendored under the hygiene rules, and the ghScrollTo helper is unconditional — programmatic scroll has exactly one owner.** lenis@1.3.11 dist (16,731 B after the sourceMappingURL strip) lives at static/vendor/lenis/ with its MIT LICENSE; base.html loads it `defer` with a pinned sha384 SRI the test recomputes from the bytes (drift fails), execution order fx-gate → motion.js → lenis.min.js → smooth-scroll.js. `window.ghScrollTo(el, block)` is defined UNCONDITIONALLY (before the rich-only guards) and drives `__lenis.scrollTo` when the instance exists, else the pre-F5 native `scrollIntoView` (fx-aware behaviour, scroll-margin-top honoured) — a bare helper call site would otherwise ReferenceError on every lite/none/touch device, where the guards return early. Lenis initialises only under data-fx="rich" AND fine pointer + hover (touch off), `anchors: false` (motion.js keeps owning same-page anchors) with `autoRaf: true`, and NEVER re-checks prefers-reduced-motion (D-LOOP-16a — an initial defence-in-depth line violated the single-gate rule and was removed in-build). base.css carries the three official Lenis classes so native `scroll-behavior: smooth` stands down only while `html.lenis-smooth` is set. Frozen-file touches are justified by the F5 contract ("replaces the scrollIntoView hack"): motion.js's anchor handler routes through the helper keeping its native branch (+3 lines), search-map.js's two call sites (pin→row 'center', Map pill 'start') route through it and its now-dead local `smoothOk()` copy is removed (fx awareness centralised); L1's two affected tests were updated to the new wiring with the behaviour contract intact and both neighbours re-verified E3 (L1 pin click scrolled 5→886 and flashed its row; G1 hide/return under Lenis re-run r27_e3_g1.py PASS). Audit clarification banked: Django `truncatewords` appends " …" — the L3 contract "description ≤ 28 words" counts content words; the ellipsis is punctuation (r29 audit script excluded it after flagging 29-token rows).
